newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa extended early losses to end moderately lower Thursday, pressured by speculative and trade selling, floor sources said.
The market hovered just below unchanged for much of day in thin, rangebound dealings, but a sell-off late in the day pushed prices toward session lows.
But with only an estimated 4,095 lots changing hands, and prices stuck to a narrow range between $1,373 and $1,400 a tonne basis March, traders said interest in the market remained muted.

March futures fell $9 a tonne on the day, to $1,380, having traded from $1,391 to $1,378. May ended down $7, to $1,402. Spot December finished unchanged at $1,327. With December set to go off the board Friday, its open interest was only four lots.
Technically, traders continued to see the $1,373-1,372 level as strong support. Nearby resistance was pegged at $1,395, with the $1,400 seen as a key psychological hurdle.
On the fundamental side, UK-based PCR Ltd managing director Robert Fish said the Ivory Coast's total cocoa production in the 1996/97 season is likely to be at least one million tonnes.
Fish's forecast comes on the heels of an estimate by a senior Ivorian diplomat, who said 1996/97 cocoa output was likely to be between 850,000 and 900,000 tonnes.
Traders expect a clearer crop picture from the Ivory Coast to emerge next month.
Elsewhere, Malaysia is expecting its 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) cocoa crop to reach 130,000 tonnes, up from an estimated 126,000 tonnes in the previous season, a government official said on Thursday.
